Sources: L18 = birchbark No. 508 (Janin 1979, book:254935 §242) and L28 = birchbark No. 506 (Janin 1997, book:624953 §1362), both from the estate of the priest and icon painter Olisei Grechin, turn of the 12th-13th c. (§244, §1362). Per Janin §1362 the series consists of baptismal (calendar) names of real commissioners/worshippers, so the names have bearers in a Novgorod record before 1230. L201 = Life of Alexander Nevsky (book:857568 §733), Pelgusy baptized as Philip, 1240. The README claim 'Russian records of the 12th-13th c.' holds.

Historical judgment: Петр, Феодор, Филипп, Анна, Мариамна, София, Федосия, Улияна, Пелагия, Оводокия and Мирофа are attested baptismal names in Novgorod records c. 1200 and are not anachronistic for 1230-1260. Мирофа is female, consistent with the already approved catalog row nov_name_mirofa_v1 (Chaykina 2006, female calendar names, grade A). The colloquial nominative forms Оводокия (Евдокия) and Улияна are acceptable for an ordinary pool and match the forms already used in the Novgorod pool from the same evidence line.

Rule application: basis calendar_rule, confidence C, period c1230, period_cap 1260, people_derivation candidate_origin, rule_basis_refs book:849577 §435 (mass baptism of Karelians 1227) + book:857568 §733 (Pelgusy/Philip). Every note says this is a calendar transfer, not a direct ethnic attestation and not a Russian fallback. This matches D61 item 1.
